query: For eutectic high-entropy alloys intended for structural applications, what single intervention could simultaneously increase strength and ductility? Formulate one testable hypothesis specifying the intervention, its proposed mechanism, the expected improvement relative to an appropriate baseline, the conditions under which it should hold, prior evidence supporting it, and an experiment that could falsify it.

evidence_appraisal.reason: Similar class of materials, but different elements

generation.hypothesis: Phase-selective recrystallization can increase strength and ductility in eutectic high-entropy alloys
generation.material_initial_state: As-cast or wrought eutectic high-entropy alloy
generation.intervention: Phase-selective recrystallization through cold rolling and annealing
generation.conditions: Room temperature, quasi-static uniaxial tensile tests
generation.structural_mediator: Uniform elongation and engineering ultimate tensile strength
generation.mechanism: Derived from materials-science principles, based on the idea that phase-selective recrystallization can refine grain structure and reduce defects, leading to improved strength and ductility
generation.predicted_outcome: Uniform elongation of ∼30% and engineering ultimate tensile strength approaching ∼2.0 GPa
generation.baseline: As-cast or wrought eutectic high-entropy alloy without phase-selective recrystallization
generation.boundary: Limited to eutectic high-entropy alloys with specific compositions and processing states
generation.uncertainty: Dependent on the specific composition and processing state of the alloy

falsification_experiment.design: Quasi-static uniaxial tensile tests on as-cast and phase-selectively recrystallized eutectic high-entropy alloys
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the phase-selectively recrystallized alloy does not show improved strength and ductility compared to the as-cast alloy, the hypothesis is falsified

Own digest: Paper card. Question: How can the limited ductility of eutectic high-entropy alloys (EHEAs) be overcome to achieve ultra-ductility while maintaining high strength?. System: Ni30Co30Cr10Fe10Al18W2 (at%) eutectic high-entropy alloy consisting of FCC and B2 phases; industrial A357 casting aluminum alloy. Processing: Two cycles of 30% cold rolling followed by annealing at 1200 °C for 20 mins with water quenching; for A357: two cycles of 15% cold rolling at 540 °C for 40 mins followed by two cycles of 30% cold rolling at 540 °C for 40 mins. Test conditions: Quasi-static uniaxial tensile tests at room temperature with an initial strain rate of 1 × 10−3 s−1; in situ tensile tests in FE-SEM; loading-unloading-reloading tests for back stress measurement.
